title: Werwolves
summary: "Werwolves" by Elliott O'Donnell is a detailed examination of lycanthropy, particularly the myths and beliefs surrounding werewolves, written in the early 20th century. It presents a blend of anthropological discourse and supernatural elements that aim to dissect the concept of metamorphosis from human to wolf. The opening portion delves into the definition of a werwolf, highlighting the complexity and various interpretations of the phenomenon across cultures and times. The narrative further explores how these beliefs are fueled by delusions and societal fears, while also hinting at the existence of actual anomalies that could be classified as werewolves, thus setting the stage for a thorough exploration of lycanthropic mythology and its implications in human culture.
